low to moderate soil sodium (Na) levels stimulated root growth and shoot potassium (K) uptake in wheat (Triticium aestivum L.), particularly in K-efficient genotypes, and increased leaf K concentration, photosynthesis, and stomatal conductancy to measured values similar under adequate K and no Na supply.
K-efficient and Kinefficient cultivar differ in their response to varied Na supply and that the response is mediated through varied K use efficiency.

low to moderate soil sodium levels may improve the growth of wheat under K deficiency.
the K-inefficiency of wheat cultivars is not related to their sensitivity to Na.
low to moderate soil sodium (Na) levels (25,50 mg Na/kg in the soil) can be used as a tool to enhance K uptake by wheat, particularly in K-ineffcient cultivars.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
low to moderate soil sodium levels can be used as a K source to enhance K uptake by wheat especially in K-efficient cultivar.
low to moderate levels of Na supply in K-deficient soils may improve wheat yield through increasing K uptake and shoot K concentration and through increasing photosynthesis.
low to moderate soil salinity (Na) can stimulate plant growth by improving K nutrition, especially in K-efficient cultivar.
The main takeaway from our work is that
low to moderate soil salinity can increase wheat K uptake and K use efficiency, and thus can improve crop yield.
